territorial_scope.description: Applies as a state statute of Idaho, enacted by the Idaho Legislature.

evidence.quote: Be It Enacted by the Legislature of the State of Idaho:

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Idaho HB 575 (2024) adds Idaho Code 18-6606, making it a crime to knowingly disclose explicit synthetic media of identifiable people without consent, with intent to harass or degrade them, or to threaten disclosure for money. Misdemeanor, or felony for repeat violations within five years. Effective July 1, 2024.
summary.long: HB 575 adds Idaho Code 18-6606 to Chapter 66, Title 18. A person commits the crime by knowingly disclosing explicit synthetic media (a) knowing or reasonably should know the identifiable person did not consent and that disclosure would cause substantial emotional distress; (b) intending to annoy, terrify, threaten, harass, humiliate or degrade that person; or (c) possessing it and threatening disclosure to obtain money. A violation is a misdemeanor, or a felony with up to ten years' imprisonment and/or a fine up to $25,000 if the person was previously found guilty of a similar offense within five years. Synthetic media is AI-created or altered content that realistically misrepresents an identifiable individual; explicit synthetic media depicts sexual conduct, intimate parts or bodily fluids. Exemptions cover lawful criminal investigations, reporting unlawful conduct, public-interest disclosures, scientific or educational purposes, and certain court proceedings. Interactive computer, information and telecommunications services are not covered for third-party content unless they intentionally aid or abet disclosure. A severability clause is included; the act takes effect July 1, 2024 under an emergency declaration.

notes: The bill addresses only a person and designates no named firm or public body; no authority is given enforcement or designation powers beyond the criminal provisions. Section 1(5) exemptions apply only to subsection (1)(a), not to (1)(b) or (1)(c). Section 2 is an emergency clause stating the act takes effect on and after July 1, 2024. The document is the bill text and records no passage dates; the adopted status comes from registry metadata. Section 1(3) cross-references prior findings of guilt in another state or local jurisdiction within five years.

"Disclose" means to make available by any means to any person.
"Explicit synthetic media" means synthetic media that depicts or appears to depict:

"Identifiable individual" means a person who is portrayed in whole or in part in synthetic media and who is recognizable by the person's face, likeness, or other distinguishing characteristic, such as a unique birthmark or other recognizable feature.
"Intimate parts" means the nude genitals, pubic area, anus, or postpubescent female nipple.

"Realistically" means that the synthetic media is sufficiently convincing such that an ordinary person viewing the synthetic media would conclude that it is an actual image or video of the identifiable person
"Sexual conduct" means actual or simulated sexual intercourse, oral-genital contact, manual genital contact, genital-anal contact, oral-anal contact, or other physical-genital contact.
such as artificial intelligence, to realistically misrepresent an identifiable individual as engaging in conduct in which the identifiable individual did not engage.
"Valuable consideration" includes but is not limited to sexually explicit images or video from the identifiable individual portrayed in the synthetic media.
an interactive computer service, as defined in 47 U.S.C. 230(f)(2)
an information service, as defined in 47 U.S.C. 153
a telecommunication service, as defined in section 61-121(2) or 62-603(13), Idaho Code

obligations.summary: Prohibits a person from knowingly disclosing explicit synthetic media in three circumstances: (a) disclosure of an identifiable person's explicit synthetic media where the person knows or reasonably should know the person did not consent and disclosure would cause substantial emotional distress; (b) disclosure intended to annoy, terrify, threaten, intimidate, harass, offend, humiliate or degrade an identifiable person; (c) possessing and threatening to disclose such media to obtain money or other valuable consideration. Violation is a misdemeanor, or a felony on a prior conviction (subsections 2-3). Exemptions in subsection (5) and the intermediary carve-out in subsection (6) apply.
obligations.applies_from: On and after July 1, 2024 (Section 2 of the Act)
obligations.conditional_on: Knowing conduct; for (a), knowledge or reasonable knowledge of non-consent and substantial emotional distress; for (c), possession plus a threat made with intent to obtain money or other valuable consideration; not applicable to the exemptions in subsection (5) or to interactive computer, information or telecommunication services under subsection (6) for content provided by another person, unless the provider intentionally aids or abets disclosure.
